modelDefinition.name: PlexCustomObjectRecord
modelDefinition.description: Vendor-shaped projection of CustomObjectRecord from /platform/custom-objects/v1/data/{customObjectName}/{id}. Generated from the PLEX dictionary 2026-08-05, not hand-written. Read-only evidence: every field is nullable because a vendor's required flag describes their write contract, not what their read endpoint returns. Harmonization happens in the hub tenant.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Primary id (== dedupeKey). Ours, not the vendor's.

fields.name: recordIdentifier
fields.description: The value used to uniquely identify a custom object record.

fields.name: createdDateTime
fields.description: The timestamp from when the record was created.

fields.name: modifiedDateTime
fields.description: The timestamp from the last time the record was modified.

fields.name: customFields
fields.description: The custom fields and values for a custom object. The customFields property is an object with a schema derived from the relevant custom fields. Each property is the name of a custom field (not case sensitive) with a corresponding value matching the custom field's type. Custom Field Type to JSON Type Mapping Boolean - boolean Custom Object Reference - object Date - string(date) Date Time - string(date-time) Decimal - number(double) Integer - integer(int64) Standard Object Reference - object Text - string Time - string(time) Custom Object Reference Format Custom Object References are always returned to the client as an object with three properties OR null. Properties id - string(uuid) - The uuid used to uniquely identify a custom object record. recordIdentifier - integer(int64) - The value used to uniquely identify a custom object record. displayValue - string - This is either the object's Primary Field (when specified) or the object's first field. When adding or updating a custom object reference, several formats can be used. A string(uuid) representing the record's ID. Example { "customFields": { "MyCustomObjectReference": "d13023f2-9841-4439-8f8b-2d75ef3e87f4" } } A integer(int64) representing a record identifier. Example { "customFields": { "MyCustomObjectReference": 15 } } An object with either a recordIdentifier or id property. Additional properties (such as displayName) are ignored with write operations. Example { "customFields": { "MyCustomObjectReference": { "recordIdentifier": 15, "id": "d13023f2-9841-4439-8f8b-2d75ef3e87f4", "displayValue": "Blue" } } } Standard Object Reference Format Standard Object References are always returned to the client as an object with two properties OR null. Properties recordIdentifiers - object - An object of identity keys and their values that uniquely identify a standard object record. This object has a schema that is derived from the identifiers used by the referenced standard object. For example, the Part standard object has a single identifier named Part_Key. displayValue - string - The human readable text used to represent the referenced record. This value alone may not uniquely identify a record. When adding or updating a standard object reference, several formats can be used. An object with the proper recordIdentifiers object. Additional properties (such as displayName) are ignored with write operations. Example { "customFields": { "MyPartReference": { "recordIdentifiers": { "Part_Key": 1234 }, "displayValue": "4799-AAA" } } } When the referenced object only has one identifier, the single value may be used. Example { "customFields": { "MyPartReference": 1234 } }

fields.name: externalId
fields.description: Native key in the source system. Half of the upsert key, so a re-extract overwrites rather than duplicates.

fields.name: sourceSystemId
fields.description: FK to ExternalSystem — WHICH instance of this ERP said so. Two sites running the same vendor are two systems, and their keys collide by construction.

fields.name: sourceSystem
fields.description:
The registered source system this row came from. A REAL relation, not a bare id: it makes `row.sourceSystem { name }` traversable and makes the platform reject a source system that does not exist — which is the difference between catching a mistyped system on the first row and discovering it after a million rows have landed under a name nobody recognises.

     One-way by design. ExternalSystem is a platform/ACE model this generator does not own, so it gets no reverse collection — and a collection of several thousand vendor models hanging off one registry row would be unusable anyway.

fields.name: sourceUrl
fields.description: Collection endpoint this row was read from, so a suspect field can be traced to the contract that produced it.

fields.name: sourceVersion
fields.description: Dictionary stamp this model was generated from. A vendor schema change shows up here before it shows up as a bug.

fields.name: syncedAt
fields.description: When this row was last read from the source.

fields.name: rawPayload
fields.description: The verbatim vendor record. Stays in the SPOKE tenant — feature bundles cross to the hub, raw payloads never do.
